annotations.annotation_text: (Latin) In ancient Rome, the tripudium was a solemn ceremonial dance.[1] The word denotes a triple stroke, in which the Earth is stamped three times with the foot.[2] Joyce does not italicize the word, treating it as an English borrowing.

annotations.target_phrase: diebus ac noctibus iniurias patiens ingemiscit.
annotations.annotation_text: (Latin) days and nights it [Creation] sighs patiently over injustices.[4] A quotation from the Commentary on the Epistle of Blessed Paul to the Romans, long attributed to Saint Ambrose but now ascribed to a contemporary of his styled Ambrosiaster. The comment is to Romans 8:22, For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now,[5]
